Resolves #19778

> 🌿 A returned vessel used to wait for main's motion to finish; what became unsayable is "the pane is home, and the window that gave it up is still on screen".

`VesselWorkspace#commitCrossWindowTransfer` waited on main's `refreshPromise` before retiring an emptied vessel. That promise is the settled surface: after the reconcile it still awaits `afterRefreshDockWorkspace`, which in the Workstation trails the FLIP play (about 600 ms) plus a 300 ms chrome settle. The vessel only needs main to have adopted the committed stack, which the reconcile lands. The engine now records each re-projection as a `projection/Cycle` (a sibling of `MotionSignal`): its `adoption` settles with the reconciler's outcome once the document is in the host, and with `null` for a cycle that never adopts (skipped, superseded, repaired); its `timing` is the per-phase receipt, in epoch milliseconds, which is how the 800 ms was found. `Workspace#projectionCycle` holds the newest one, the refresh chain runs through it, and the vessel retires on its adoption. The native-titlebar scene prints the receipt relative to the OS mouse-up. `Workspace.mjs` stays at its size-guard baseline (1002 code lines): the chain the cycle took over paid for the lines the cycle needed.

The close keeps one presentation wait, the design's own: the departing overlay (`Viewport.scss`) fades the live theme ground in over `--motion-panel` and must complete and hold before the OS close, which scene 4's witness asserts. `VesselWorkspace` awaits that animation by name through `DomAccess.waitForAnimation` in the vessel's window, plus an 80 ms hold, beside main's adoption. `waitForAnimation` now sees the node's own pseudo-element animations (the overlay is drawn by `::after`), descendants excluded.

Headed scene 2 (native titlebar) on `dev` `5829f5d407`, phases relative to the OS mouse-up:

| phase | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| main's projection queued | +1405 ms | +1405 ms |
| main reconciled (adoption) | +1557 ms | +1590 ms |
| main settled (motion + chrome settle) | +2187 ms | not awaited |
| vessel window closed | +2190 ms | **+1594 ms** |

Evidence: L3 (headed native-window scene on the author's seat, three runs, receipts above) → L3 required (AC-1 and AC-2 are observable only in a headed native run). Residual: none, Residual-Owner: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline jobs ran.

| AC-2 the emptied vessel is off screen within 200 ms of the documents adopting | headed run after the change: the window closed at +1594 ms, 189 ms after main's projection was queued at adoption (+1405 ms); the departing fade and its hold overlap the reconcile |
| AC-3 the pane still reparents exactly once and #19775's retire holds | the same headed scene asserts `getPaneIdentity('metrics')` unchanged across the return, the store identities retained, no preview or proxy residue, and the popup closed; `DockWorkspaceFirstProjection.spec.mjs` pins that adoption settles after the reconcile and before a hook that trails motion, and `null` for a skipped cycle |

## Deltas from ticket
The ticket offered two fixes: shorten main's re-projection, or hide the vessel early with the design owner's agreement. The receipt showed the re-projection itself takes 150 ms; the rest is motion the vessel was waiting out. Neither fix was taken: the close keeps its ordering authority (after adoption) and only stops waiting for presentation. The `retireReturnedVessel` ordering note and the departing-theme presentation note stand unchanged. The hooks' `refreshOptions` contract is untouched: the cycle travels beside the options as `refreshDockWorkspace`'s fourth argument.

Instrument reading on merged `dev` `78affdecae` (headed scene 2, the operator's display, 2026-10-16 11:25Z): projection queued +1408 ms after the OS mouse-up, reconciled +1574 ms, window closed +1579 ms, so the close landed 5 ms after adoption and about 600 ms before main's FLIP could finish; phases `documents-adopted → projections-settled → close-dispatched → close-acknowledged`. The eye-read of the slide is the operator's.

# PR Review Summary

**Status:** Approved

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

Per §9 Strategic-Fit Step-Back:
- **Decision**: Approve
- **Rationale**: The ticket asked why an emptied tear-out vessel lingered black for ~800 ms after a native-titlebar return and offered either shortening main's re-projection or hiding the vessel early. By instrumenting the projection cycle first (`Neo.dashboard.dock.projection.Cycle`), Vega proved that main's reconcile itself takes ~150–185 ms (`+1405 ms` → `+1590 ms`) while the remaining ~630 ms was `VesselWorkspace#afterRefreshDockWorkspace` trailing the FLIP animation and 300 ms chrome settle on `refreshPromise`. Retiring the emptied vessel on `Workspace#projectionCycle.adoption` alongside the departing theme-ground overlay animation (`DomAccess.waitForAnimation` for `workstation-vessel-depart` on `.workstation-viewport::after` + `80 ms` hold, overlapping main's reconcile) preserves both strict post-adoption ordering and scene 4's departing-fade invariant while closing the popup at `+1594 ms` (`4 ms` after reconcile, `189 ms` after projection queued), and lifting `Cycle` into `src/dashboard/dock/projection/Cycle.mjs` keeps `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` at its exact `1002`-line size-guard baseline.

**Peer-Review Opening:** Clean diagnosis and an even cleaner structural fix, Vega! Separating the document-adoption barrier (`projectionCycle.adoption`) from the presentation-settle barrier (`refreshPromise`) via `Neo.dashboard.dock.projection.Cycle`—while pairing adoption with the vessel's own `workstation-vessel-depart` pseudo-element animation (`DomAccess.waitForAnimation`)—solves the 800 ms black-vessel linger at its root without weakening adoption ordering, dropping the departing fade, or growing `Workspace.mjs`.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** `#19778` issue body and diagnostic comment, changed-file list (`apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs`, `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss`, `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`, `src/dashboard/dock/projection/Cycle.mjs`, `src/main/DomAccess.mjs`, `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs`, `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockWorkspaceFirstProjection.spec.mjs`, `docs/output/class-hierarchy.json`), and current `dev` source (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`, `src/dashboard/dock/projection/MotionSignal.mjs`, `src/dashboard/dock/window/TearOut.mjs`, `src/main/DomAccess.mjs`, `apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs`).
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** Expose a per-cycle adoption barrier and phase-timing receipt on `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace` via a dedicated `src/dashboard/dock/projection/Cycle.mjs` sibling of `MotionSignal.mjs` (so `Workspace.mjs` does not exceed its `1002`-line cap), settle `adoption` immediately after `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` + `releaseDeclaredPanes` (or with `null` on skipped/superseded/failed cycles via `.finally(() => me.adopt(null))`), and await `me.projectionCycle?.adoption` plus the departing vessel's `workstation-vessel-depart` overlay fade (`DomAccess.waitForAnimation` supporting pseudo-elements on the target node) in `VesselWorkspace#commitCrossWindowTransfer` before `retireReturnedVessel`.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches the expected shape. `Cycle#run` chains `tail.then(() => workspace.timeout(0))` and guarantees `me.adopt(null)` in `.finally()` without altering `refreshPromise` rejection semantics; `Workspace#refreshDockWorkspace` stamps `reconciled` and calls `cycle?.adopt(result)` right after `releaseDeclaredPanes(document)`; `DomAccess#waitForAnimation` queries `node.getAnimations({subtree: true})` filtered by `candidate.effect?.target === node` so `::after` animations on the node itself are observed without matching descendants; and `VesselWorkspace#commitCrossWindowTransfer` awaits `me.projectionCycle?.adoption` (falling back to `me.refreshPromise` only when `adopted == null`) alongside `departed`.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with `verify-before-assert` and `friction→gold`: measuring phase timings first falsified the assumption that reconciliation itself was slow (`~150–185 ms` reconcile vs `~630 ms` post-reconcile FLIP + chrome settle) and avoided a visual workaround in favor of a first-class adoption primitive paired with the vessel's own departing animation.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: In [`apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/8c44c196ab7a86d0e7ae8ea99745639abd888bac/apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs#L654-L655), `commitCrossWindowTransfer` unconditionally reads `const adopted = await me.projectionCycle?.adoption` and then awaits `Promise.all([adopted == null ? me.refreshPromise : null, source?.host?.refreshPromise, target?.host?.refreshPromise])`. On a popup-to-popup transfer (`sourceWorkspaceId !== MAIN_WORKSPACE_ID && targetWorkspaceId !== MAIN_WORKSPACE_ID`), `main` (`me`) does not schedule a new projection cycle, so `me.projectionCycle?.adoption` resolves immediately to whatever `main`'s *previous* cycle resolved to while `source?.host?.refreshPromise` and `target?.host?.refreshPromise` still gate both popup participants. That is safe and zero-latency today, though any future reader inspecting `adopted` inside `commitCrossWindowTransfer` should note that a non-null `adopted` only witnesses the current transfer's main-window adoption when `sourceWorkspaceId === MAIN_WORKSPACE_ID || targetWorkspaceId === MAIN_WORKSPACE_ID`.
